A person's wound was exposed to some bacteria and then bacterial growth started to happen at the same place. The wound was later treated with some antibacterial medicine and the rate of bacterial decay(r) was found to be proportional with the square of the existing number of bacteria at any instance. Which of the following set of graphs correctly represents the 'before' and 'after' situation of the application of the medicine?

[Given: No. of bacteria, time, bacterial growth follows order kinetics.]
en.explanation:
Before the medicine, growth is first order: .

At , , and the ratio then rises exponentially, so the 'before' plot is an exponential curve starting from 1 on the axis; a curve starting from 0, as in (B), is ruled out.

After the medicine, the rate of decay is , so the plot of against is a parabola through the origin that bends upward. A straight line, as in (A), would mean , and a falling curve, as in (D), would mean decreases as grows.

Only option (C) shows an exponential rise from together with an upward parabola from the origin.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
